classification: Causal boundary audit of already exposed sh5, not a fresh holdout or candidate tuning set.
question: Can the R22 outgoing base-axis momentum continuity mechanism legitimately repair the R17/R19 sh5 load-handoff false rise or improve actual load transfer?
required_reproduction: Rerun the R19 support-weighted controller with its registered Coupled detector on stock sh5. Reproduce all four G4 clauses, final-20ms table support, tracking, peak force, saturation, tool timing and the 3.903s false rise. Record the decisive detector channel at 3.900--3.903s.
compatibility_gate: The R22 release state may be proposed only if it is already a state used by this controller or registered detector, acts on the same decisive physical channel, and can change actual command/support. Do not install an R10-only optional detector on this controller, bypass Coupled, mask an alarm, or infer load transfer from detection.
causal_crosschecks: R19 support-weighted removal of the information COM action
decision: If the compatibility gate fails and the crosschecks do not identify a unique pre-release actuator coordinate, report the tested boundary. Do not create a new gain or threshold from sh5 outcome.
next_valid_experiment: A future control law must preregister a public pre-release physical coordinate, change actual table support or closed-loop sensor state, pass exposed normals first, then protected collisions/holdouts without retuning.
